title: Add a JSON output mode to the word count tool
summary: The counting library gets one function that writes the counts as a JSON object, and the command line reads the new option and chooses between the two output functions.

design_elements.title: Write the counts as a JSON object
design_elements.responsibility: Turns the three counts into the text of one JSON object with the keys lines, words and characters, in that order, with no other text.

design_elements.title: Read the JSON option and keep the old path
design_elements.responsibility: Reads the --json option, prints the JSON text when it is present, leaves the plain line and the error messages as they were, and ignores a repeated option.

decisions.title: Write the JSON text by hand
decisions.choice: Build the JSON text with the standard library, because the tool has no dependencies and the object has three numeric fields.
alternatives: Add a JSON library as a dependency.
Print the counts with a format string in the main program only.
decisions.consequences: No new dependency is needed. The formatter lives in the library, so a unit test can check it without running the program.

risks: The option parser may change how an unknown option is reported, so the existing usage tests must still pass.
